summary: This function reads configuration from a Dockerfile and Docker Compose file, extracts key information like the parent image, volume mappings, and exposed ports, then generates and prints a Mermaid diagram that visualizes how these components connect together.

explanations.6: Path() creates a reference to a file path; it doesn't read the file yet, just represents where it is.
explanations.14: The .exists() method checks if the file actually exists on disk before we try to read it.
explanations.16: re.search() looks for the first match of a pattern in the text; the pattern r"FROM\s+(.+)" finds the word FROM followed by whitespace and captures whatever comes after it.
explanations.18: from_match.group(1) retrieves the captured part (everything after FROM), and .strip() removes leading/trailing whitespace.
explanations.22: yaml.safe_load() parses the YAML file into Python dictionaries and lists, so you can access the data like nested objects.
explanations.23: The .get() method safely retrieves a value from a dictionary, returning an empty dict {} if the key doesn't exist, preventing errors.
explanations.25: This extracts the left side of a volume mount (before the colon), which is the local folder path; for example, 'docs:/app' becomes 'docs'.
explanations.27: str() converts the port number to a string so it can be included in text later.
explanations.38: The f-string prefix lets us insert the parent_image variable directly into the text using curly braces.
explanations.51: "\n".join() combines all the lines in the mermaid list with newline characters between them, creating one multi-line string to print.
